task.instruction: Find the top story from BBC News in the technology section for today.

final_answer:
The top story in BBC News' Technology section is **"Global stocks plunge as fears over US AI slowdown spread to Asia and Europe"** (the article page's own headline reads "Global tech stocks plunge as US midterms add to AI slowdown fears"). It is the lead item on the Technology front page and the newest story there — timestamped "19 hours ago," i.e. Friday 6 November 2026, by business reporters Rachel Clun, Osmond Chia and Nick Edser. Nothing newer is published in the section today (the next items down are marked "24 hrs ago" and "8 days ago").

Global stock markets tumbled as investors sold tech shares on fears that the US midterm elections will slow AI development. The tech-heavy Nasdaq fell 5.5% on Thursday, with the sell-off spreading to Asia on Friday — Japan's Nikkei closed down 6%, South Korea's Kospi plunged more than 8% at one point, triggering a circuit breaker, before closing down 6% — and European markets opening lower (FTSE 100 down nearly 2%, Dax down 2.4%). The "magnificent seven" tech companies including Apple, Nvidia and Tesla shed a trillion dollars in a single trading day, with Nvidia sliding more than 9%; SpaceX and Tesla fell 8% and nearly 11% respectively. The Nasdaq lost an estimated $2.5tn (£1.9tn) in market value and is now in correction territory.

Investors are worried about tougher AI regulation after Democrat candidates opposed the data centres the technology depends on, adding to existing doubts about whether the huge sums being spent on AI will pay off — as AJ Bell's Dan Coatsworth put it, there is "no clear idea of when, or whether, there will be payback."

judge.rationale: The agent read BBC Technology, identified the lead story, opened it, and final page evidence supports the headline “Global stocks plunge…” timestamped 19 hours ago.

final_page.title: Global tech stocks plunge as US midterms add to AI slowdown fears
